text:
sophia: Quick thread to nail the beta seat allocation + minimum acceptance criteria for the new "engagement" design partners. Need something lean we can publish internally.

kevin_pm: Goal: make intake + gating repeatable. Proposal: single form, 20-min triage call, and a 10-day PoC window. If PoC passes automated evals, they get a full seat.

anna_eng: For PoC pass: must call Redwood API end-to-end, demonstrate handling of failures (retries/429), and show sample latency at expected QPS. If they can't hit endpoints or have flaky infra, mark as "needs infra work".

tom_cs: Add a customer impact filter: they must show one measurable metric they expect to move (e.g., CSAT lift, deflection %, answer time). If vague, deprioritize.

raji_research: We'll run a tiny eval battery on their PoC: 12 prompts across hallucination-prone cases, out-of-distribution inputs, and long-context behavior. Return a short report (pass/fail + notes).

kevin_pm: Signals we'll capture during beta: API calls/day, fail-rate, avg latency p50/p95, prompt-level quality score (0-4) sampled weekly, and partner response rate to check-ins. Keep it to 6 metrics.

samir_ops: Ops limits: first wave max 7 partners. Seats allocated by intake score (0-30) where we weight integration readiness and potential impact highest. Need a simple scoring sheet.

eng-ops-bot: reminder: current onboarding capacity this sprint: 5 seats. Update intake tracker to claim.

sophia: Triage scoring suggestions? Keep it usable by CS or PM on a quick call.

tom_cs: Scoring idea (each 0-5): Integration readiness, Business impact, Compliance readiness, Owner bandwidth, Infra blockers, Strategic priority (override). Sum -> seat rank. Auto-reject if Integration readiness = 0.

anna_eng: Also capture routing: hosted vs dedicated vs private. If they require private, they go to sales/enterprise path not beta. Add field in intake: "deployment mode required".

raji_research: For quality checks include a simple golden/expected outputs field in intake so we can map automatic evals. If they can't provide, we still run our evals but note limitations.

kevin_pm: Public partner-facing blurb (3 bullets): 1) Timeline & commitment (2-6 weeks, weekly check-ins), 2) What we provide (seat, evals, engineering touchpoints), 3) What we expect (PoC, feedback, usage signals). Short and prescriptive.

samir_ops: Escalation: if partner misses 2 weekly syncs or PoC drift >7 days, we move them to "paused". Seat freed after 3 missed events. Exceptions for strategic deals only with sales sign-off.

kevin_pm: Drafting the intake now. Minimal fields: org, contact, product use-case, expected tokens/QPS, required SLA, deployment mode, sample prompts/golden outputs, compliance needs, desired start week, priority rationale.

raji_research: I'll prepare the 12-prompt eval and a template 1-page report.

anna_eng: I'll make an engineering onboarding checklist: API keys, rate limits, model pinning, KV cache settings, monitoring hooks, and a sample load test script.

tom_cs: I'll build a one-page CS scoring sheet for calls + a template email to invite partners to the PoC window.

samir_ops: I'll confirm the exact seat count and add the data retention / logs policy checkbox to the intake form.

eng-ops-bot: task created: /tasks/ENG-BETA-ONBOARDING assigned to kevin_pm, anna_eng, tom_cs, raji_research, samir_ops 12:00 tomorrow.

sophia: Great. Let's aim to publish the internal onboarding doc before EOD tomorrow. Keep the partner email short and set clear expectations. Ping me if you hit a blocker.
